entries.behavior: A compute-only client sends no storage heartbeat until its first memory segment mount, after which heartbeat starts automatically.
entries.reason: Rust exposes health/background workers and memory mounting, but has no test or lifecycle wiring proving that the first memory mount automatically starts heartbeat while a zero-segment client remains idle.

entries.behavior: A compute-only client starts storage heartbeat automatically after its first local-disk mount.
entries.reason: Rust records local-disk mount state for remount but does not prove that mounting local disk automatically activates the background health heartbeat.

entries.behavior: In non-HA mode, a mounted client reconnects after the Master restarts on the same address and automatically remounts its segment.
entries.reason: Rust implements ping-triggered remount logic, but no test restarts a non-HA Master at the same address and proves the background client reconnects and republishes its mounted segment.

entries.behavior: With P2P handshake and no memcpy override, reading a complete replica mounted by the same client automatically uses the LOCAL_MEMCPY strategy and returns exact bytes.
entries.reason: Rust implements local endpoint registration and a direct-copy branch, but no test drives a P2P client Get through strategy selection and proves both exact data and local-memcpy dispatch.

entries.behavior: With metadata discovery, a replica advertised under the client's local host alias is recognized as local even when it differs from the transport endpoint and is read with LOCAL_MEMCPY.
entries.reason: Rust registers local segment aliases, but has no metadata-mode Get test proving alias locality, differing transport endpoint, direct-copy strategy, and payload integrity together.

entries.behavior: Two P2P clients on the same TCP host but with different endpoints treat each other's replicas as remote and use TransferEngine rather than local memcpy.
entries.reason: Rust locality is keyed by exact segment name, but no two-client P2P test proves that same-host/different-port endpoints are not collapsed into local memcpy and that the remote transfer succeeds.

entries.behavior: Two metadata-discovered clients on the same TCP host but with different host aliases treat each other's replicas as remote and use TransferEngine.
entries.reason: Rust has no metadata-mode two-client test proving distinct aliases remain remote through Get strategy dispatch and return the exact payload via TransferEngine.

entries.behavior: For both P2P and metadata handshakes, a hot-cache hit redirects a nominally remote memory replica to LOCAL_MEMCPY and returns the cached bytes.
entries.reason: Rust hot-cache unit tests cover cache operations, but no client Get test supplies a remote replica and proves cache-hit redirection, strategy choice, and payload integrity in both handshake modes.
